source: Re-anchored on 2026-11-26 to 28854775e5965eb554b368cc3a543969a635b681, the round-5 head the protocol review and the Nov 13-14 trials scored, per Brandon's Nov 25 decision. The commits after it on the branch (7793d1e4, 6ff2ed04, and the head 674071a9 the key previously named) fix m2, m3 and m4, so a finding of any of the three at the later head is a false positive, and 661-m1's accepted citations are not in the body the merged head carries. Each finding's spans were re-read at the re-anchored tree; the liveness entries are checked in CI against the anchor's own worktree.

findings.summary: The pull request body's CI and stack lines are stale.
findings.source: The location is pull_request.body. At the round-5 head the body's gate line still cited the pre-rebase head's run (`gate` on `61273b4f` (run 43429340358)), which is the stale-CI defect the Nov 14 trial recorded; the merged body later updated that line to `674071a9` (run 43510666665). The pre-rebase stack sentence (`pre-rebase head `61273b4f`) predates the round-5 review. The eval input is the round-5 body, shipped as 661-round5-body.md beside this key: GitHub does not expose pull-request body edit history, so that file is reconstructed from the merged body with the gate line reverted to the round-5 values and the sentences that describe post-round-5 commits removed; the provenance note in the file lists each deviation. A citation counts when the quote contains one of the two lines.

findings.summary: An unreadable log file is reported as "1 line" could not be parsed.
findings.source: At this head `unreadable = 1` (coordinator.py 734-735, inside `_review_context`, 712-752) charges a wholly unreadable log file to the unreadable-line count, so the omission reads "1 line(s) could not be parsed" (rounds.py 202-203) instead of naming the file, and no file-level omission exists. 6ff2ed04 later made an unreadable file its own omission ("the round log file could not be read"), which is why the key's previous anchor 674071a9 had no live m2. prior_blocks is rounds.py 162-220.

liveness.text: f"{unreadable} line(s) could not be parsed",

findings.summary: break instead of continue hides a current-head round.
findings.source: The budget loop (rounds.py 180-182) walks newest-first and `break`s at the first record that does not fit, so a current-head record behind a superseded one that does not fit is hidden; `continue` would keep scanning. 6ff2ed04 later split the loop by head ("Skip a superseded round that does not fit"), which is why the key's previous anchor 674071a9 had no live m3. prior_blocks is rounds.py 162-220.

liveness.old:
if used + len(text) + (2 if kept else 0) > budget:
            break
liveness.new:
if used + len(text) + (2 if kept else 0) > budget:
            continue

findings.source: The gate is rounds.py 207-215, `if record.findings_omitted and record.head_sha == current_head`, and the `and record.head_sha == current_head` conjunct is unpinned at this head: dropping it survives the anchor's own full test suite (the same failures as the baseline). 6ff2ed04 later added `test_a_superseded_truncated_record_does_not_block_a_new_head`, which kills the drop, which is why the key's previous anchor 674071a9 had no live m4. prior_blocks is rounds.py 162-220.
